subject: RSHE
title: Big feelings and helpful steps
objective: Name a big feeling and a way to manage it.
objective_verbatim: Name a big feeling and a way to manage it.
display_objective: Name a big feeling and a way to manage it.
weekly_outcome_verbatim: Name a big feeling and a way to manage it.
calendar_note: Year A. Spring 1 Week 2, 11–15 January 2027. Wednesday 13 January 2027, P1. One 40-minute formative lesson for three to four learners. Spring 1 runs 4 January–12 February for six weeks; Week 6 is assessing. No clock time supplied.
source_adaptation: C65 outcome retained verbatim. Inherited named source programmes, resources and accredited units in A64/D64/E64/F64 replaced with generic feelings scenarios, familiar school-agreed help and evidence-record wording. Four original unnamed fictional cases and original four-picture bank. Word banks, starters and visible models retained on all seven tasks. No medical, diagnostic, therapeutic or accredited-outcome claim. No personal account required; first-person sentence frame is practice using fictional or picked words.

sources.note: Exact B65 and C65 verified. Inherited A64 strand qualifier and D64–F64 identifying alignment/resource details rendered generically. Raw workbook not distributed. Owner supplies date, group, access and six-week calendar.
Accepted BUILD RSHE Spring 1 format, both editions, Shared_Resources, Level 2 aids, short chunks and private help. Current lesson is new row-65 content with original generic feelings artwork.

Wednesday 13 January 2027 P1, 40 minutes, Year A, group three to four. Four invented big-feeling scenes, familiar agreed help choices, word bank/starter/visible model on every task, 10–15-minute chunks and scribed route. Practice When I feel…I can… with story or picked words only; no personal disclosure or public questions. Generic private help and safeguarding route. Pause for Downloaded.

source_end_check: Name a stated big feeling in an invented example and choose one safe, familiar way to manage it.
timing: 6 guided match; 3 private hinge; 3 help choice; 1 reset.
source_timing: No fixed lesson minutes in row 65; owner specifies 40 minutes and 10–15-minute chunks.

routes.Supported: One short story line at a time. Keep word bank, sentence starter and visible model. Offer two feeling/help choices, pointing, aid, drawing or faithful scribe. Same name-a-feeling-and-help goal. Record any answer cue.
routes.Independent: Use a chosen story, word bank, starter and visible model. Name the stated feeling and choose a safe familiar strategy. Normal reading, communication or scribing access remains. No personal story required.
routes.Aspire: Keep all Level 2 aids. Explain a safe choice or show that more than one strategy might fit. Use the same short practice line; more writing or personal disclosure is not required.

colour_blind_safe: Feeling labels, story words, numbered pictures, strategy labels and clear text carry meaning; no colour-only answer codes.

feelings.label: cross
feelings.text: A young person waits for a turn. They say, “I feel cross.” Their hands feel tight.
feelings.model_line: When I feel cross I can tell someone.

feelings.label: sad
feelings.text: A young person sees a mark they did not plan on a drawing. They say, “I feel sad.” Their body feels slow.
feelings.model_line: When I feel sad I can tell someone.

feelings.label: worried
feelings.text: A young person will try a new short task. They say, “I feel worried.” Their tummy feels tight.
feelings.model_line: When I feel worried I can tell someone.

feelings.label: excited
feelings.body_clue: The body may want to move.
feelings.text: A young person will start a fun task. They say, “I feel excited.” Their body wants to move.
feelings.model_line: When I feel excited I can move.

strategies.label: breathe
strategies.pupil: Use the calm breath step you know, with help if needed.
strategies.staff: Use only the school’s already familiar, agreed breath routine. No breath-holding, counts, depth demands or compulsory practice. If uncomfortable or unhelpful, stop and choose another option.

strategies.label: move
strategies.pupil: Use a small safe move that is agreed with an adult.
strategies.staff: Use the existing agreed movement option in a safe space, with usual support and sensory/physical adaptations. Do not introduce exercise demands.

strategies.label: tell someone
strategies.pupil: Tell a trusted adult. You can ask in private.
strategies.staff: Use the school’s help route to an available trusted adult. Speech, aid, pointing, writing or exact scribe valid; seek another adult through route if first is busy.

strategies.label: take space
strategies.pupil: Ask to use the agreed quiet place, with help.
strategies.staff: Use the school’s agreed supported pause/quiet space. Let the adult know; do not send a pupil away alone or imply leaving supervision. Keep a supported return available.

body_clue_rule: A face or body clue may go with a feeling. It does not prove the feeling. People can look or feel different. Use the words in the invented story; do not diagnose or guess a real person’s feeling.
matching_rule: All four strategies can be possible, depending on the person and the school’s agreed version. Prepared pairs are examples, not one right match. Accept another safe choice with a short explanation or selection. No promise that a feeling will go away.
response_rule: Use the invented story or picked feeling/strategy words to practise the line. No personal account or current-feeling question. Drawing a story face/help step, pointing, voice, aid or exact scribe is valid; record the chosen feeling and safe strategy, not drawing skill. Read back and permit correction.
help_route: Point to HELP, write or ask to talk in private with a trusted adult through the school’s help route. If one adult is busy, use the route to another. Pass, pause and supported return available.
disclosure_note: If a pupil discloses, listen calmly, reassure and pass the concern to the safeguarding lead through the school’s procedure. Do not probe or promise secrecy. Keep details out of this pack and shared evidence.
private_help_route: Point to HELP, write or ask to talk in private with a trusted adult through the school’s help route. If one adult is busy, use the route to another. Pass, pause and supported return available.
scribed_route: Let the learner point to a story feeling/help word, use an aid, draw or speak. Record exact selection, read back quietly and permit correction. Label a drawing through the learner’s choice; do not grade art or infer feeling from a face. Record access separately from supplied thinking.
worked_example_and_fade: Read A’s quote “I feel cross.” Point to cross. Tight hands are a stated possible clue, not proof or a diagnosis. Model “When I feel cross I can tell someone.” For B/C/D offer a bank, short frame and A model; reduce answer cues only. Normal reading, drawing, communication and scribing aids stay available.
prompt_ladder: 1 Point to place/instruction. 2 Ask a short question privately. 3 Rephrase. 4 Offer scaffold/choice. 5 Model first step only, then return task. Allow processing. Input: point to the stated word; guided match: accept safe options; individual work: keep all Level 2 aids and log actual help.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: one line, labelled images, four simple words and short choices. Communication and Interaction: literal text, wait time, familiar aid, pointing/drawing or exact scribe. SEMH: calm third-person scenes, private turns, predictable resets/pass/return. Sensory and Physical: uncluttered print, comfortable seat, normal aid and agreed supported space/movement. EAL: plan in any language. Numbers and words carry meaning; colour optional.
misconceptions: A face proves the feeling: correct with the story quote and body-clue rule. One feeling has one right help step: offer more than one safe possibility. A step must make the feeling go away: it may help, with support/time. A big feeling is wrong: acknowledge it; judge naming and safe help, not the feeling itself.

main_hinge.claim: A face or body clue may go with a feeling; use the invented story words, not the picture as proof.

parallel_hinge.claim: Choose a safe familiar help step; it does not have to make the feeling go away.

success: Name one stated feeling in an invented story.
Choose one safe, familiar strategy or ask a trusted adult for help.
Practise the line or record a story drawing/selection with a faithful scribe.

evidence.description: Dated individual story/picked-word feeling-and-help response, using book, aid, story drawing or faithful scribe. Keep stated feeling, safe strategy, first response, actual access and answer cues, one next step and reply.

assessment: Secure: names a stated big feeling and a safe familiar way to manage it. Partial: names feeling or help but not both. Not yet: needs further modelling. Unobserved: pass or no collected response. Alternative safe matches accepted with a short explanation/selection. Drawing skill, disclosure and practising a technique are not conditions.
where_this_leads: This helps me name a feeling in a story and choose safe help when a task or plan feels hard in learning or future work.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Wednesday 13 January 2027 · P1 · 40 minutes · Year A
BUILD · three to four learners · Spring 1 Week 2 · formative
Theme: Resilience & Change. Six-week term; Week 6 assessing.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T none).
Name a big feeling and a way to manage it.
Source: BUILD Weekly - Spring, PSHE & Citizenship, row 65. B65 Spr1·W2 and C65 exact. Named framework/resource context is rendered generically. No accreditation or therapeutic claim.

Name cross, sad, worried or excited in calm invented scenes. Use a stated feeling rather than diagnosing a face/body clue. Choose a safe, already familiar school help step. Match by possibility, not one fixed pair. Practise “When I feel… I can…” with a fictional scene or picked words, not a personal disclosure.

Books, pencils, Support Cards and Vocabulary Mat; usual aids and staff evidence record. Face cards are reference pictures. Body clues, help steps and scenes are editable text. Confirm the school’s familiar breath, movement and supported quiet-space options, available trusted adult and help route. No new technique, compulsory practice or public response.

Wednesday 13 January 2027 P1, Year A. The owner supplies the date and timetable. Spring 1 Week 2 runs 11–15 January. Theme Resilience & Change; six teaching weeks, Week 6 assessing. The exact C65 outcome is used; identifying source resource labels are generic.
This helps me name a feeling in a story and choose safe help when a task or plan feels hard in learning or future work.
6 guided match; 3 private hinge; 3 help choice; 1 reset.

Chunks last 12, 13 and 15 minutes. Two one-minute resets are included in the total. Reduce repetitions for access. Keep word bank, starter and visible model on every task. No question asks for a learner’s own current feeling.

0–3 calm arrival and starter: use story A words, choosing cross or sad privately. 3–7 pre-teach the four feeling words and four familiar school help steps. A picture/body clue may fit many feelings; story words state the feeling. 7–11 model A: cross, tight hands, tell a trusted adult; show the written line. Privately check feeling and help. 11–12 reset with familiar neutral option.

12–18 guide B/C/D one short line at a time. Match a stated feeling and possible safe help; accept more than one safe match. 18–21 main private hinge B: a face/body clue may fit but does not prove a feeling; use the story words. Parallel A: choose a safe help step; do not claim the feeling must go away now. If unclear, point to the quote, re-model and check privately. 21–24 choose a familiar help step without requiring practice. 24–25 reset.

25–34 each chooses one invented scene and names the feeling plus a safe help step. Use “When I feel… I can…” for the story/picked words, not personal history. Drawing a story face or help step with labels, pointing or exact scribe is valid. 34–37 one next step and response. 37–40 private exit names a feeling/help pair. A pass is unobserved. All seven task scaffolds remain visible on Support Cards.

Each of seven tasks has a short bank, starter and visible model in Support Cards. These stay on all routes: Starter, Model check, Guided match, Private hinge, Help choice, Individual line or drawing, Feedback and exit. Repeat exact model wording as a reference, never as prefilled learner evidence.

One short story line at a time. Keep word bank, sentence starter and visible model. Offer two feeling/help choices, pointing, aid, drawing or faithful scribe. Same name-a-feeling-and-help goal. Record any answer cue.

Use a chosen story, word bank, starter and visible model. Name the stated feeling and choose a safe familiar strategy. Normal reading, communication or scribing access remains. No personal story required.
Keep all Level 2 aids. Explain a safe choice or show that more than one strategy might fit. Use the same short practice line; more writing or personal disclosure is not required.

Read A’s quote “I feel cross.” Point to cross. Tight hands are a stated possible clue, not proof or a diagnosis. Model “When I feel cross I can tell someone.” For B/C/D offer a bank, short frame and A model; reduce answer cues only. Normal reading, drawing, communication and scribing aids stay available.

Let the learner point to a story feeling/help word, use an aid, draw or speak. Record exact selection, read back quietly and permit correction. Label a drawing through the learner’s choice; do not grade art or infer feeling from a face. Record access separately from supplied thinking.

1 Point to place/instruction. 2 Ask a short question privately. 3 Rephrase. 4 Offer scaffold/choice. 5 Model first step only, then return task. Allow processing. Input: point to the stated word; guided match: accept safe options; individual work: keep all Level 2 aids and log actual help.

Pupil pages are reference cards, not write-on sheets. Use a book, usual aid, drawing or faithful scribe. Do not copy all source text. Plan in any language. No task asks for personal/current feelings or a public account.

Offer A feeling choices cross/sad, and safe help choices tell someone/breathe. Key feeling cross from the quote. Either familiar safe help can fit; model tell someone. Ask privately or use pointing. Re-model the quote and line if needed.

Main key B: a face/body clue may fit a feeling; it does not prove it. Story words state cross. A false option says the face proves the feeling. Parallel key A: choose a safe help step. The false option says the feeling must go away now. Leave bank/starter/model visible. Pass/silence unobserved; re-model and recheck privately.

Cognition and Learning: one line, labelled images, four simple words and short choices. Communication and Interaction: literal text, wait time, familiar aid, pointing/drawing or exact scribe. SEMH: calm third-person scenes, private turns, predictable resets/pass/return. Sensory and Physical: uncluttered print, comfortable seat, normal aid and agreed supported space/movement. EAL: plan in any language. Numbers and words carry meaning; colour optional.
Point to HELP, write or ask to talk in private with a trusted adult through the school’s help route. If one adult is busy, use the route to another. Pass, pause and supported return available.

If a pupil discloses, listen calmly, reassure and pass the concern to the safeguarding lead through the school’s procedure. Do not probe or promise secrecy. Keep details out of this pack and shared evidence.

A face proves the feeling: correct with the story quote and body-clue rule. One feeling has one right help step: offer more than one safe possibility. A step must make the feeling go away: it may help, with support/time. A big feeling is wrong: acknowledge it; judge naming and safe help, not the feeling itself.

One dated individual story response or drawing/selection with the chosen feeling and safe familiar help step. Keep story reference, first response, usual access, supplied thinking, next step and reply. A faithful point/aid/scribe record is valid. Do not infer a real-life coping performance from a story line.

Secure: names a stated big feeling and a safe familiar way to manage it. Partial: names feeling or help but not both. Not yet: needs further modelling. Unobserved: pass or no collected response. Alternative safe matches accepted with a short explanation/selection. Drawing skill, disclosure and practising a technique are not conditions.

One next step: name the story feeling or add a safe help step. Keep first try and reply separate. VF verbal feedback; WS with support; I own thinking; NS next step; // self-edit; ? read back; E actual saved evidence. R only after Voice, Audience, NS and response in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode.

Evidence Sheet page 1 is a book-task reference; page 2 private staff record with blank entries. No prefilled answers or personal concern details. Read exact scribing back. Offer to Communication portfolio; staff confirm any accredited mapping.

Spring 1 Week 2 is formative; Week 6 assessing. Builds on recognising that change can feel hard by naming a big feeling and safe familiar help. No clinical advice, treatment claim, promised emotional outcome or requirement to demonstrate coping.
Only BUILD RSHE Spring 1 Week 2 authored. No later weeks or separate RSE content. Pause for Downloaded.

Theme Resilience & Change. Formative. Six-week term, Week 6 assessing.

Use four calm invented scenes: cross, sad, worried and excited. Match a stated feeling with safe familiar breathe, move, tell someone or take space. More than one safe match may fit. Trusted adult/school help route; pass, pause and supported return. Exact scribe reads back. Plan in any language.

Name a big feeling and a way to manage it.

Name a stated big feeling and choose a safe familiar school strategy in a third-person invented scene. No diagnosis, disclosure prompt or compulsory practice. Face/body clues are possibilities, not proof. No promise that a technique removes a feeling.
cross is stated in the quote. Hands may feel tight. Possible safe help: breathe or tell someone. When I feel cross I can tell someone.
sad is stated in the quote. The body may feel slow. Possible safe help: tell someone or take space. When I feel sad I can tell someone.
worried is stated in the quote. The tummy may feel tight. Possible safe help: tell someone or breathe. When I feel worried I can tell someone.
excited is stated in the quote. The body may want to move. Possible safe help: move or take space. When I feel excited I can move.

Main B: a face/body clue may fit but does not prove a feeling; use the words. Parallel A: choose a safe help step rather than claim the feeling must go away now. Model check: A says cross; tell someone or breathe may fit. No public hands-up check. Re-model the quote/frame and recheck privately. A pass is unobserved.

All four strategies can be possible, depending on the person and the school’s agreed version. Prepared pairs are examples, not one right match. Accept another safe choice with a short explanation or selection. No promise that a feeling will go away.

For invented D: “When I feel excited I can move.” A safe agreed take-space or tell-someone option may also fit. The first-person sentence is practice for the story or picked words, not a request for a personal account. A drawing/label/point/aid/scribe naming feeling and safe help has the same goal.
Bank: cross, sad. Starter: The story says ... . Visible model: Story A says, “I feel cross.”
Bank: cross, tight, tell. Starter: The feeling is ... . Help is ... . Visible model: Story A: “When I feel cross I can tell someone.”
Bank: sad, worried, excited, breathe, move, tell, space. Starter: The story says ... . They could ... . Visible model: Story A: cross; tell someone. Other safe help can fit.
Bank: words, face, may, help. Starter: A clue may ... . The words say ... . Visible model: Story A states cross. A face alone is not proof.
Bank: breathe, move, tell, space. Starter: They could ... . Visible model: Story A: “They could tell a trusted adult.”
Bank: cross, sad, worried, excited, breathe, move, tell, space. Starter: When I feel ... I can ... . Visible model: Story A: “When I feel cross I can tell someone.”
Bank: feeling, help, ask. Starter: A feeling is ... . A safe step is ... . Visible model: Story A: cross; tell someone in private.
Record the learner’s chosen words exactly, read back privately and allow correction. Keep usual aid separate from supplied answers. No current-feeling question or public retelling.
Use only the school’s already familiar, agreed breath routine. No breath-holding, counts, depth demands or compulsory practice. If uncomfortable or unhelpful, stop and choose another option.
Use the existing agreed movement option in a safe space, with usual support and sensory/physical adaptations. Do not introduce exercise demands.
Use the school’s help route to an available trusted adult. Speech, aid, pointing, writing or exact scribe valid; seek another adult through route if first is busy.
Use the school’s agreed supported pause/quiet space. Let the adult know; do not send a pupil away alone or imply leaving supervision. Keep a supported return available.

A face proves feeling: use the story words. One fixed match: accept safe alternatives. Help must remove feeling: it may help, with support and time. Big feelings are wrong: judge naming and safe choice, not the feeling. Drawing skill is not assessed.

Supported, Independent and Aspire all retain the seven Level 2 banks, starters and visible models. No route needs personal disclosure or a coping demonstration. Read, point, draw, aid, type or faithful scribe valid; plan in any language.

Keep actual feeling/help response, usual access, content cues, first try, NS and reply. E saved evidence; R after Voice, Audience, NS and response. Offer to Communication portfolio; staff confirm mapping. Formative Week 2; Week 6 assessing.

If a pupil discloses, listen calmly, reassure and pass the concern to the safeguarding lead through the school’s procedure. Do not probe or promise secrecy. Keep details out of this pack and shared evidence.
